title: Change in HbA1c and CGM Metrics Following Hybrid Automated Insulin Delivery (AID) Therapy in Type 1 Diabetes Mellitus
summary:
Background
People with type 1 diabetes need to adjust their insulin treatment on a daily basis according to their glucose levels. Modern automated systems can take over part of this task. Studies conducted under controlled conditions have shown that these systems can improve glucose control. However, less is known about how well they perform in routine clinical practice and whether outcomes differ between the various systems available.

Research Question
This study investigates how glucose control changes during the first year after adults with type 1 diabetes transition to an automated insulin delivery system. In addition, the study explores whether outcomes differ between systems and which individuals benefit most from the transition.

Methods
Data from adults with type 1 diabetes who transition to an automated insulin delivery system at a specialized diabetes outpatient clinic in Germany are analyzed. Participants receive routine clinical care throughout the study period. Glucose outcomes before system initiation are compared with those obtained one year later. In addition, changes in glucose control over the first 3, 6, 9, and 12 months and every 3 months up until 2 years after AID initiation are evaluated, and outcomes are compared across the different systems used.

interventions.name: Treatment with one of the automated insulin delivery (AID) systems approved for use in Germany
